There are 60 minutes in an hour.

Regarding the competitor analysis, Streamline Autos' direct-to-consumer (DTC) model presents a significant strategic threat to traditional automotive sales structures. By eliminating the dealership layer, they reduce overhead costs, allowing for more competitive pricing that can attract price-sensitive consumers. Furthermore, their direct engagement creates a closed-loop data system, enabling rapid iteration of product features and marketing messages based on real-time consumer behavior.

For our business, this implies a need to reassess our value proposition. If we rely on traditional dealership margins, we may struggle to match their pricing. We should consider accelerating our own digital transformation efforts, such as enhancing online purchasing capabilities or adopting a hybrid sales model. Additionally, we must prioritize building direct customer relationships through digital channels to capture the same behavioral insights they are gaining, ensuring we do not lose market share to their agile, data-driven approach.
